figures.caption: Fig. 3: Reliability diagrams show foreground probability calibration for each SWIFT configuration. Gray bars show empirical foreground frequency, orange shading shows the calibration gap, and the dashed line denotes ideal calibration. SWIFTe-LDE4 achieved the lowest ECE and Brier score, illustrating that calibration and segmentation overlap are distinct objectives.

Fig. 2: Representative predictive-entropy maps across six test cases. The top row shows the image with manual and automated contours; remaining rows show entropy maps for SWIFT, SWIFTe, SWIFTe-LoRA, and SWIFTe-LDE4. Yellow indicates higher entropy, and panel numbers denote sDSC.

Fig. 1: Pretraining context and transfer results. Left: CT10K pretraining subset used for SWIFT encoder pretraining and its scale relative to VoCo. Right: detection, sDSC, ECE, and Brier score across full fine-tuning, efficient decoder (EffiDec), LoRA adaptation, and LDE4 for SWIFT and VoCo.
Fig. 5: Radiomic-feature agreement across the SWIFT progression. Panel (a) shows median manual-versus-automated CCC by IBSI feature family; panel (b) shows the fraction of features with CCC ≥ 0.75.
